How do you build a Notion OS with Claude? One board: every idea lands there and Claude writes the script, what goes on screen and the camera angle. The same workspace holds content, career, learning and travel, and it tracks the creators I watch.

guide: This sets up a Notion workspace where one board holds every idea and Claude drafts the script, on-screen shots and camera angle for each; you need a Notion account and Claude (the app or Claude Code) with access to Notion.
1. In Notion, create one database called "Ideas" with properties for status, type (content, career, learning, travel) and a link field.
1. Add a short template page to each entry with headings for Script, On-screen shots and Camera angle.
1. Connect Claude to your Notion workspace using the Notion connector (MCP), and give it access to that database only.
1. Ask Claude to build the rest of the workspace: separate sections for content, career, learning and travel, each linked back to the Ideas board.
1. Whenever you drop a new idea on the board, ask Claude to fill in the Script, On-screen shots and Camera angle sections on that page.
1. Add a second database listing the creators you follow, and have Claude check their latest posts and write a short summary for each into Notion.
1. Create trip pages in the travel section and use Notion's share option to send any page to someone as a link.
Watch out: Claude can edit anything you give it access to, so share only the databases it needs and duplicate your workspace as a backup before the first big build.

```
You are helping me build a personal operating system in Notion, using the Notion connector you have access to. I have a Notion account and I use <Claude or ChatGPT>. Please do the following, and show me the plan before you change anything.
1. Create an "Ideas" database with properties for status, type (<content, career, learning, travel>) and link. Give every new entry a page template with the headings Script, On-screen shots and Camera angle.
2. Create a section for each type: <list your sections>. Link each one back to the Ideas database.
3. Create a "Creators" database for <the creators or accounts I follow>, with a field for their latest posts and a short summary.
4. Create a "Trips" section where each trip is its own page I can share by link.
Constraints: only touch pages inside <name of the parent Notion page>; do not delete or rename anything that already exists; ask me before any change that affects more than ten pages.
Return a short summary of every database and page you created, with its link, and a note on what I should check by hand.
```
